requirements: No refuse, garbage, abandoned vehicles, or overgrown brush, weeds or trees
Sidewalks and driveways free of holes; no standing stormwater
Foundation, walls, chimney, roof shingles and gutters in good repair
Porches, landings, stairs, balconies and railings safe
No broken glass or doors; windows and doors working
Working smoke detectors and CO detector
Central heating, air conditioning, kitchen, baths and light fixtures in working order
Property tax, sewer and property code fee balances are checked by Borough staff

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Certificate of Property Compliance form (and the Fire Safety Certificate form for a sale) and pay at Borough Hall, 723 West Atlantic Avenue, payable to the Borough of Laurel Springs. Inspectors are notified by email only after payment is received. Fees are non-refundable. The inspector leaves a copy at the property.

evidence.quote: Whenever there shall occur a change in occupancy in any residential property, including one- and two-family homes and apartments, a new certificate of property compliance shall be required. A change in occupancy shall occur in an apartment by a change in tenant or by the execution of a new lease with a new tenant, and in all other dwelling units by sale or lease.
In the case of the resale of a property, both a Certificate of Property Compliance and Fire Safety are required.
Payment  - must be received at Borough Hall before the inspector(s) are notified via email.
Certificates of Property Compliance expire 45 days from the date of inspection
Does owner possess a valid lead-safe certificate for this property?
Whenever there shall occur a change in occupancy in any residential property, including one- and two-family homes and apartments, a new certificate of occupancy shall be required.
evidence.doc_date: Code 193-4B, amended 9-8-2025 by Ord. No. 901-2025 (ecode360, legislation through 07-13-2026)

resale_co.notes: Re-checked October 20, 2026; page, forms and fees unchanged. Borough Code 193-4B (Property Maintenance, read on ecode360) requires a new certificate on any change in occupancy, including sale of a one- or two-family home, with application at least 10 days before the change; 193-4C says fees are in the Annual Fee Ordinance and depend on time left before the new occupant. Ord. No. 901-2025 (Sept 8, 2025) added 193-4B(4): an extension may be granted for a property in uninhabitable disrepair once all forms and fees are filed and no one lives there; the buyer then pulls permits and must pass a property compliance inspection before occupancy. The page says to see the Annual Fee Schedule; the forms leave fee amounts blank for staff, so fees here come from the Fire Prevention / Property Maintenance page. The Inspector may issue a Conditional CPC letter allowing construction permits first, with no occupancy during construction. Contacts (mailto links on the page): Property Maintenance Officer Dominic Krawchuk (dkrawchuk@laurelsprings-nj.com); Permit Clerk Cindy Cheeseman (ccheeseman@laurelsprings-nj.com). Rental CPC has the same fee tiers (rental program). Code 193 also has vacant property registration ($500 initial).

requirements: Working smoke alarms on every level including basement and within 10 feet of bedroom doors; type depends on build year (hardwired and interconnected for newer homes, in every bedroom for 1991/1992 and later)
Hardwired smoke detectors may not be replaced with battery units; interconnected detectors must be replaced with compatible ones
Basement detector within 10 feet of the stairway, not in the stairway
Two-family homes: detectors at each landing of common hallways and stairs
Do not place detectors within 5 feet of a kitchen, 3 feet of fans, bathroom doors or supply vents, or 1 foot of a light fixture; detectors must not be painted
Central-station monitored alarm systems must be certified by a licensed NJ Fire Protection Contractor before the Fire Marshal's inspection
CO alarm on each sleeping level, in the hallway near every bedroom door, if there is a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage

fire_cert.notes: Fire Marshal: Kenneth J. Cheeseman, 856-784-0500 ext. 25, kcheeseman@laurelsprings-nj.com. The DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) lists Laurel Springs as 'F' (Fire Department); the Borough runs it as the combined Office of Fire Prevention and Property Maintenance. Borough Code 137-11B (Ord. No. 644-2005) still lists older smoke certificate fees of $35 / $70 / $125 (more than 10, 4 to 10, and under 4 business days); the Borough page shows the current $45 / $90 / $161, which match the state fees, so the page amounts are used. The fire certificate expires 45 days from inspection, shorter than the usual state 6 months. The Fire Safety form checks only smoke and CO detectors; no extinguisher rule is published, although the Code 137 Article II title still mentions fire extinguishers.
